FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Automotive Braking Systems Sectional Committee had been approved by tbe Transport Engineering Division Council. This Indian Standard was first published in 1964. The present revision was considered necessary on the basis of experience gained in the manufacture and testing of friction materials. The brake lining of braking system of automotive vehicles is considered as of significant importance becauseof their role in overall safety of vehicle. The requirements laid down in this standard are to be used as quality control parameters on brake linings, both as inplant control by the lining manufacturers and for quality assessment procedure It is accepted that the actual values of the various parameters can be finalizedL by tbe purchasers. only after carrying out tests on trial production batches and shall be agreed between the supplier and the purchaser for each approved type of lining. This Indian Standard is one in the series of standards being developed for brake linings of automoThe other parts are: tive vehicles. Automotive vehicles - Brake linings ( Rubberized ) : Part 2 SpecifiIS 2742 ( Part 2 ) : 1994 cation Automotive vehicles - Brake linings : Part 3 Methods of test IS 2742 ( Part 3 ) : 1994 Automotive vehicles - Brake linings : Part 4 Coefficient of IS 2742 ( Part 4 ) : 1994 friction - Method of test IS 2742 ( Part 5 ) : 1994 Automotive vehicles - Brake linings : Part 5 Internal shear strength - Method of test The following Indian Standards are important adjuncts to this standard: Automotive vehicles - Braking systems - Performance requireIS 10376 : 1982 ments for mopeds IS 11716 : 1986 Automotive vehicles - Braking systems - Performance requirements for scooters and motorcycles IS 11852 ( Parts 1 to 7 ) : Recommendation for brakes and braking systems for automotive 1987 vehicles IS 13670 : 1992 Automotive vehicles - Three wheelers - Brake performance requirements The committee responsible for the preparation of this standard is given in Annex A.

For tbe purpose of deciding whether a particular requirements of this standard is complied wtih, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

4.1 The finished brake lining shall be free from defects, such as cracks, scoring, indentations, unevenness or other defects affecting its life and serviceability.

1

IS 2742 ( Part 1 ) : 1994 4.2 The frictional characteristic of the linings as declared by the lining manufacturers shall be maintained throughout the life of the wearing portion. 4.3 The linings shall conform to the requirements stipulated when tested any time within a year of normal storage provided the linings are stored according to the lining manufacturer's recommendations. In case of bonded linings, they shall have such qualities as to permit it to be bonded with a suitable adhesive. 5 SAMPLING Unless otherwise agreed upon manufacturer and the purchaser, scheme shall be in accordance ( Part 1 ) : 1992. 6 DIMENSIONAL TOLERANCES between the the sampling with IS 2500 7 TEST REQUIREMENTS 7.1 The following properties shall be specified' by the manufacturer.
